slot.brief: Compare the sign and magnitude of susceptibility and relative permeability for diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials; select the correct statement about their field-line behaviour.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the magnetic susceptibilities and relative permeabilities of diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials, and their effect on magnetic field lines?
options: Diamagnets have small negative susceptibility and relative permeability below $1$; they weakly expel field lines, while paramagnets and ferromagnets attract them, the latter more strongly.
Diamagnets have small positive susceptibility and relative permeability above $1$; they attract field lines, while paramagnets have negative susceptibility.
Paramagnets have large negative susceptibility and relative permeability below $1$; ferromagnets have small positive susceptibility and relative permeability just above $1$.
All three have positive susceptibility and relative permeability above $1$; they attract field lines to the same extent.

verdicts.working: Diamagnets have small negative susceptibility and μᵣ<1; paramagnets have small positive susceptibility, while ferromagnets have large positive susceptibility and attract field lines more strongly.

working:
$\mu_r=1+\chi_m$. Diamagnets: $\chi_m<0$ (small), $\mu_r<1$; paramagnets: $\chi_m>0$ (small), $\mu_r>1$; ferromagnets: $\chi_m\gg0$, $\mu_r\gg1$. Field lines are weakly expelled by diamagnets and concentrated by paramagnets and more strongly by ferromagnets.

Independent check: Diamagnets have small negative susceptibility and μᵣ<1; paramagnets have small positive susceptibility, while ferromagnets have large positive susceptibility and attract field lines more strongly.
